he: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר נָתַן לַשֶּֽׂכְוִי בִינָה לְהַבְחִין בֵּין יוֹם וּבֵין לָֽיְלָה:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא עָשַֽׂנִי גּוֹי:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא עָשַֽׂנִי עָֽבֶד:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא עָשַֽׂנִי אִשָּׁה:
(נשים אומרות: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם שֶׁעָשַֽׂנִי כִּרְצוֹנוֹ:)
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם פּוֹקֵֽחַ עִוְרִים:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם מַלְבִּישׁ עֲרֻמִּים:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם מַתִּיר אֲסוּרִים:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם זוֹקֵף כְּפוּפִים:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם רוֹקַע הָאָֽרֶץ עַל הַמָּֽיִם:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם שֶׁעָשָׂה לִי כָּל־צָרְכִּי:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם הַמֵּכִין מִצְעֲדֵי גָֽבֶר:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אוֹזֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּגְבוּרָה:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם עוֹטֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּתִפְאָרָה:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם הַנּוֹתֵן לַיָּעֵף כֹּֽחַ:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם הַמַּעֲבִיר שֵׁנָה מֵעֵינָי וּתְנוּמָה מֵעַפְעַפָּי:

וִיהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּ֒פָנֶֽיךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ שֶׁתַּרְגִּילֵֽנוּ בְּתוֹרָתֶֽךָ וְדַבְּ֒קֵֽנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתֶֽיךָ, וְאַל תְּבִיאֵֽנוּ לֹא לִידֵי חֵטְא וְלֹא לִידֵי עֲבֵרָה וְעָוֹן וְלֹא לִידֵי נִסָּיוֹן וְלֹא לִידֵי בִזָּיוֹן וְאַל יִשְׁלֹט בָּֽנוּ יֵֽצֶר הָרָע וְהַרְחִיקֵֽנוּ מֵאָדָם רָע וּמֵחָבֵר רָע וְדַבְּ֒קֵֽנוּ בְּיֵֽצֶר הַטּוֹב וּבְמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים וְכוֹף אֶת־יִצְרֵֽנוּ לְהִשְׁתַּעְבֶּד־לָךְ וּתְנֵֽנוּ הַיּוֹם וּבְכָל־יוֹם לְחֵן וּלְחֶֽסֶד וּלְרַחֲמִים בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ וּבְעֵינֵי כָל־רוֹאֵֽינוּ וְתִגְמְ֒לֵֽנוּ חֲסָדִים טוֹבִים: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה גּוֹמֵל חֲסָדִים טוֹבִים לְעַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל:

יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּ֒פָנֶֽיךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהַי וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתַי שֶׁתַּצִּילֵֽנִי הַיּוֹם וּבְכָל־יוֹם מֵעַזֵּי פָנִים וּמֵעַזּוּת פָּנִים מֵאָדָם רָע וּמֵחָבֵר רָע וּמִשָּׁכֵן רָע וּמִפֶּֽגַע רָע וּמִשָּׂטָן הַמַּשְׁחִית מִדִּין קָשֶׁה וּמִבַּֽעַל דִּין קָשֶׁה, בֵּין שֶׁהוּא בֶן בְּרִית וּבֵין שֶׁאֵינוֹ בֶן בְּרִית:
text: ( The Thirteen Principles of Faith) (1) There exists a perfect God Who created everything. (2) God is One there is only one God. (3) God cannot be viewed in bodily terms. (4) God is Eternal. (5) Jews pray directly to God with no intermediaries. (6) The prophets are true. (7) Moshe was the greatest prophet. (8) The entire Torah was given to Moshe. (9) The Torah is eternal and unchanging. (10) God knows what we do. (11) God rewards and punishes according to our actions. (12) Mashiach will come. (13) There will be Techiyas Hameisim.
But First Fifteen Thank-Yous!
FAQ: Thank you? For what? My life stinks! ANSWER: Good point! See Appendix 2
Thank You, for You give us the ability to understand the difference between day and night meaning: good and bad, right and wrong.

Instant Insight: Literally, could be translated as a rooster. The uniqueness of the rooster is that it starts to crow right before the light of dawn. Night/darkness represents a lack of clarity and a sense of hopelessness. In the morning light, we see that all is really not so bad. The rooster teaches us that even in the darkest time of night, we can see the light if we use the “ability to understand” that Hashem gave us! We thank Him for that ability.
Thank You, for You did not create me a member of another nation (who have to go through an entire process if they want to join the Chosen People. I was given that as a gift at birth thank You!). FAQ:
Thank You, for You did not create me a servant (rather, I am free to make my own choices, be held responsible for them, and thus earn reward thank You!). For women:

FAQ: Chosen People? Doesn’t this brachah sound racist? I mean, I know a lot of really nice nonJews and some “not-so-great” Jews! Is there really such a difference? ANSWER: Common misconception! See Appendix 4.
For men:
Thank You, for You created me according to Your will (and thus I have a unique and crucial role to play, even though at times it seems unclear).
Thank You, for You open the eyes of the blind (and thus I am asking You to remove my blindness to the spiritual world).
Thank You, for You did not create me a woman (and I am happy to have all those extra mitzvos!).
Thank You, for You provide clothing for the naked (we worry about the label and style but we need to be happy that we have clothes to wear!).

FAQ: This is not simply a FAQ it is the FAQ. Is it so bad to be a woman that men thank Hashem that “You did not create me a woman”? And were men not created “according to Your will”?! ANSWER: Crucial question! The complexity of these two brachos touch on the understanding of each person’s role as a contributing member of this great mission to the world called Am Yisrael. See Appendix 11 but read it all and read it slowly.

Thank You, for You free those imprisoned ( (1) imprisoned in our bodies while sleeping, with no control over our actions and thoughts by You waking us up we now have the ability to move about and make choices thank You; (2) imprisoned in physical prisons; or (3) imprisoned in the “prisons” we create for ourselves by our own insecurities). FAQ: FAQ: But I can’t “stand up straight”! I’ve tried, but I keep falling back down. All the stuff in my life is crushing me! ANSWER: OY! Difficult question! See Appendix 3.
[mrgn]FAQ: If that is true, then why should we ask Hashem for stuff?
gave me all I need! ANSWER: Good thinking! See Appendix 1.

Thank You, for You give those who are bent over (whether because of physical issues or from the difficulties and hardships in their lives) the ability to stand up straight (and deal with their struggles).
Thank You, for You establish solid ground over the waters of the deep (so we have “solid ground” upon which to build our lives).
Thank You, for You have provided me with all my needs (whatever You have given me must be what I need not more and not less even though sometimes that is hard to understand).
Instant Insight: This brachah is in the singular specifically about me (gave me all my

needs), unlike so many other brachos. Why? Because I need to feel satisfied with what I have. But regarding others, my job is not to tell them, “Don’t worry you have all you need,” but to go help them! Instant Insight: This brachah can also be understood in the following manner: all the “stuff” in life that You have “given” to me, all the things that I am going through, as difficult as they may seem, I believe they are all things that I need to deal with in order to be the best “me” I can be (even if now I cannot see how). Thank You!

Thank You, for You (1) direct our steps; and (2) support every step we choose to take. (Sometimes You set our path and direct us into certain circumstances that are growth opportunities for us, in order to help us fulfill our ultimate mission thank You! And when we make our own free will choice/ step when responding to those circumstances, You support and allow us to make those steps, for better or worse thank You!)
Thank You, for You give us courage and strength (to utilize our talents for the good).
Thank You, for You crown Bnei Yisrael with glory (by giving us the tools to give meaning and beauty to our lives).

Thank You, for You give strength and energy to those of us who are either physically, emotionally, or spiritually exhausted (so that we can keep going and make it through another day). Do not answer Amen after this brachah, as it is one long brachah until the words.
Thank You, for You woke me up physically and spiritually (for the purpose of sending me out into the world to fulfill the task You assigned to me).
FAQ: Which “steps” does Hashem decide and set for us, and which do we choose on our own? ANSWER: That is a complex issue! See Appendix 5.
Now that I’m awake, with all the gifts and tools You have given me, I ask for help to conduct myself in a way that allows me to serve You to the utmost. First: Bein Adam La’Makom

FAQ: We say, “Do not allow the yetzer hara to get the better of us,” and “Compel our creative powers to be used to serve You.” But I thought we had free will? This sounds like we are asking Hashem to eliminate our free will choices! ANSWER: Great question! See Appendix 6. FAQ: “Do for us good acts of kindness” What does that mean? Are there “bad” acts of kindness? ANSWER: Clever thinking! See Appendix 7.
